title: losos-ctl wire format
description: JSON schemas for the losos backend (lososd daemon + losos-ctl facade). The facade relays every subcommand to lososd over the system D-Bus and prints exactly one JSON object on stdout, terminated by a newline; the standalone admin UI consumes the same documents from lososd's loopback HTTP API.

mode.description: local = private LosOS Cloud (sharingMyStorage=false); mesh = contributes storage to the Longhorn pool on the edge's rke2 cluster (sharingMyStorage=true). This used to mean the Tahoe-LAFS grid; Tahoe is gone, but the two spellings are unchanged because persisted state files and the admin SPA carry them.

rebuildState.description: Lifecycle of the last/current nixos-rebuild triggered by `change`.

job.description: Opaque id returned by `change`; referenced by the detached rebuild watcher.

progress.description: 0 while building (coarse); 100 on success. Optional on the persisted state file (defaults to 0); always present in the status wire response.

message.description: Human-readable status; on failure includes the last nixos-rebuild log line. Optional on the persisted state file (defaults to empty); always present in the status wire response.

settingsResponse.description: The user-tunable losos.* options parsed out of modules/overrides.nix (line-based). Returned by `settings`; consumed by the admin UI for first paint. Lines for options LosOS no longer has (`losos.nextcloud.*`, `losos.keyring.*`, `losos.aio.*`) are ignored when read and dropped on the next apply.

sharingLocally.description: losos.sharingLocally: share as `kindashared` (uid 1004) with the local gateways of this box's own network only. Turning it on while no local gateway answers (`localGateway` false in `GET /api/edge`) is refused (HTTP 409, `{"error":"...","localGatewayRequired":true,"setting":"losos.sharingLocally"}`).

hostName.description: System hostname; systemd-resolved publishes <hostName>.local over mDNS, and Nginx routes /<service> paths on it.

proxyEnable.description: losos.proxy.enable — expose this appliance through the master proxy (a QUIC tunnel to the edge Traefik).

clusterEnable.description: losos.cluster.enable — join the edge's mesh rke2 cluster.

shareCompute.description: losos.cluster.shareCompute — contribute CPU during the window below.

computeWindowEnd.description: losos.cluster.computeWindow.end, HH:MM. end < start wraps midnight.

hardeningApparmor.description: losos.hardening.apparmor — AppArmor. Off by default; nixpkgs ships profiles for only a fraction of what runs here.

hardeningMalloc.description: losos.hardening.malloc — hardened_malloc. Off by default; covers the host's dynamically linked daemons, not the static Go binaries or anything in a pod.

hardeningNosmt.description: losos.hardening.nosmt — disable SMT. Off by default; roughly halves the core count. The baseline kernel parameters deliberately do NOT include nosmt so this stays the only way to turn it on.

hardeningUsbguard.description: losos.hardening.usbguard — block USB devices not present at boot. Off by default so a keyboard attached for console recovery keeps working.

commit.description: The commit the change made in the box's configuration repository (/etc/nixos, see backend/src/config_repo.rs), as a full sha; null when nothing changed on disk or the commit could not be made. The commit is best effort: a rebuild is queued either way, and the next sync commits whatever is uncommitted before it pushes.

job.description: Opaque id of the rebuild triggered to apply the reset.

reset.description: Always true; distinguishes the factory-reset ack from a change ack.

commit.description: The commit the change made in the box's configuration repository (/etc/nixos, see backend/src/config_repo.rs), as a full sha; null when nothing changed on disk or the commit could not be made. The commit is best effort: a rebuild is queued either way, and the next sync commits whatever is uncommitted before it pushes.

totalBytes.description: Size of the /persist filesystem in bytes (df). Null when it could not be read.

usedBytes.description: Bytes of /persist in use (df). Null when it could not be read.

reserveBytes.description: Unallocated volume-group space a grow would claim (vgs free extents times extent size). 0 once the reserve is claimed; null when the box has no persist-vg to ask.

grew.description: Whether the filesystem actually got bigger, measured rather than inferred from exit status. This is the only field worth trusting: every way a grow goes wrong goes wrong quietly, and a resize2fs run against an unresized mapping succeeds while changing nothing.

beforeBytes.description: Size of the /persist filesystem in bytes before the grow.

afterBytes.description: Size of the /persist filesystem in bytes after the grow.

claimedBytes.description: Bytes of unallocated volume-group space the logical volume claimed (free extents times extent size).

user.description: The account whose password was replaced, echoed back so a client knows which one changed. The password itself is never echoed, in any field, on any path.

changed.description: Whether the owner's password in the people file (backend/src/people.rs) was replaced. False only when the box has no owner yet, so there is nobody to change it for. A refusal is an error reply (400 / org.losos1.Error.Failed), never `changed: false`.

code.description: The appliance recovery code: a canonical lowercase v4 UUID, minted from 16 bytes of /dev/urandom on first read and stable for the life of the installation. Stored 0600 at /var/secrets/losos-recovery-code (LOSOS_RECOVERY_FILE, set by modules/recovery.nix) and persisted by impermanence's whole-/var bind mount. It survives `losos-ctl factory-reset`, which rewrites state.json and overrides.nix and does not touch /var/secrets; only a reinstall destroys it, which is the one event it exists for. There is no route that rotates it — a code the owner has written down must not be replaceable from the admin UI in one click.

minted.description: Whether *this* call created the code, so the first-run wizard can say "write this down now" once and "here it is again" afterwards. It describes the call, not persisted state: it is true on exactly one successful read per installation (or again after the file has been lost or corrupted, which lososd logs at error level because any previously written-down copy has just stopped matching).

lookResponse.description: The look of the admin pages, kept on the box as /var/lib/losos/look.json (backend/src/look.rs) so every browser sees the same thing. Not a setting: changing it writes the document and nothing else (no rebuild, no overrides.nix).

background.description: {"kind":"none"}, {"kind":"shipped","name":"tide|grid|dusk"} (a picture in the SPA bundle, /backgrounds/<name>.svg), or {"kind":"upload","version":N,"contentType":"image/...","url":"/api/look/background?v=N"} for a picture the owner uploaded. `url` is added by the render, not stored.

veil.description: How much of the page colour is laid over the picture, 20-90 percent (default 60), so text stays readable in both themes.

widgets.description: Widgets written by hand, in creation order: {"id":"w<N>" (never reused), "name", "span":"half|full", "files": [{"name", "content"}]}, index.html first. The files are the owner's HTML, style, script and data, stored verbatim and run only inside the sandboxed /widget-frame/ (see POST /api/look/widgets). A widget saved before widgets were files reads as one index.html.

shipped.description: The names of the shipped pictures, for the pane's swatches.

limits.description: {widgets, nameChars, widgetBytes, files, fileNameChars, fileKinds, imageBytes, veil:{min,max}}: what the writes refuse with 400, so the pages can check before sending.

available.description: False — with at most `reason` beside it — when the edge runs no market, this box was not cleared for it, the box has no master proxy configured, or no checked gateway is in reach. That is the normal state of most appliances, so it is a 200 and not an error.

reason.description: Present only with `available: false`, and only when the cause is one the owner can see on the Mesh pane: `noOfficialEdge`: no edge in reach passed the gateway checks (edgeResponse.official is false), so trading is off while storage sharing through them keeps working.

listings.description: What can be bought now, as the registrar's GET /market/listings returns it. Names no seller.

account.description: This appliance's own market activity, as the registrar's POST /market/account returns it: fee_bps, currency, seller_onboarded, seller_ready, can_sell_storage, can_sell_compute, listings, entitlements, purchases (each with status, expires_at and, for storage, the provisioned volume) and sales. On an edge that takes coins: coin_fees_owed (cents of platform fees owed on Bitcoin, Monero and Zcash sales), coin_fees_since (when that debt began, Unix seconds), coin_fee_credit, coin_fee_limit (cents), coin_fee_grace_secs and coin_sales_paused (true while coin payments for this seller are refused). A USDC sale's fee_offset is the part of its fee that paid coin fees owed; seller_net already leaves it out.

checkout_url.description: POST /api/market/orders only. Always plain https; the page sends the owner there to pay.

url.description: POST /api/market/onboard only: Stripe's hosted onboarding link, null once the account is ready. Always plain https.

ready.description: POST /api/market/onboard only: whether the connected account can already receive transfers.

marketActionResponse.description: The registrar's own reply to the action, plus `available`.

available.description: False, with `reason`, when this box is not offered machines. A 200 either way.

reason.description: Present only with `available: false`. `notSharing`: this box does not share its disk (losos.sharingMyStorage), and machines are offered only to boxes that do. `noOfficialEdge`: no edge in reach is one LosOS runs. `notOffered`: the edge runs no machines, or does not answer for them.

catalogue.description: The registrar's GET /market/vm-images: images (id, name, family, cloud_init, efi, disk_gib, memory_mib; no download addresses), installer_only, not_offered (family, why), shape (cpu, memory_mib, disk_gib), fee_bps (always 5000), max_replicas, max_upload_bytes, published.

listings.description: The machine listings on the shelf (kind `vm`, unit `replica-month`).

account.description: As in marketResponse, with can_host_vms, vm_fee_bps and uploads (id, name, stored, size, min_disk_gib, created_at); a machine purchase carries `vm` (image, name, address, created, halted).

machines.description: The registrar's POST /market/vms/status: per machine order, `order_id` and `replicas` (name, status: Running, Starting, Preparing, Paused, Stopped or Failed). Empty when the mesh does not answer.

available.description: Whether Lab guests can start under libvirt here. False is the normal state of a box: the helper is opt-in.

reason.description: With available:false: `off` (losos.lab.libvirt.enable is false), `notRunning` (no helper answers), `helperError`, or the helper's own sentence (libvirt did not answer, images missing).

uri.description: The libvirt URI the helper uses.

label.description: What runs the guests, for the console header: "KVM via libvirt" or "QEMU via libvirt (no KVM)".

images.description: Which of bzImage (kernel), rootfs.bin and gear.bin are in the helper's images folder.

virt.description: The second path: a raw byte relay from the WebSocket at /api/lab/virt to libvirt's unix socket for the helper's URI, for the page's own libvirt client (admin-ui/lab/virt-rpc). `available` is true when that socket accepts a connection now, whether or not `virsh` works; `socket` is its path (or the first one tried); `reason` says why not.

available.description: False, with at most `reason` beside it, when no checked gateway is in reach, the box has no master proxy configured, or the edge serves no DNS zone (its /domains routes answer 503). A 200 either way.

reason.description: With `available: false`, `noOfficialEdge`: the edges in reach are none that LosOS runs. With `eligible: false`, `stripeAccount`: this box has no Stripe connected account that is ready and carries its UUID.

eligible.description: Whether this box may add a domain: its Stripe connected account is ready (details submitted, payouts enabled, transfers active) and carries this box's UUID.

target.description: `<label>.<zone>`, this box's name in the edge's zone, where a CNAME points. Null until `eligible`.

addresses.description: The edge's public addresses, for a domain at a zone apex, where a CNAME is not allowed.

domains.description: This box's claims, each {domain, status: live|waiting, txt_name, txt_value (null until eligible), txt_found, points_here, problem: null|stripeAccount|txtMissing|txtWrong|notPointing|takenElsewhere|lookupFailed, checked_at, verified_at, wallet: null|found|unsigned|cname|other|missing}. `wallet` is what the edge last saw of the wallet record at the domain itself, while a wallet is bound.

box.description: This box's id on the edge, as the wallet binding message names it.

zone.description: The edge's DNS zone, as the wallet binding message names it.

names.description: This box's names in the edge's zone: its hostname when that lies inside the zone, and `target` once eligible. They carry the wallet record while a wallet is bound.

wallet.description: The wallet bound to this box's names: {address, bound_at, record, published, published_at}, where `record` is the TXT value (`ENS1 dnsname.ens.eth 0x…`) the edge publishes at `names` and the owner may add at a domain of their own, and `published` maps each name to what public DNS showed of it when the edge last looked (`found`, `unsigned`, `other`, `missing`; a name not looked up yet is absent), at `published_at`. Null when none is bound.

domainsResponse.description: The edge's view of this box's custom domains (edge/registrar/src/domains.rs), plus `available`. The same document answers GET, add and remove.

target.description: endpoint, bucket, prefix, region, accessKeyId, hasSecret and storageClass; never the secret.

last.description: {time, snapshot, files, bytes} of the last successful backup.

job.description: {kind: backup|restore, job, state: running|done|failed|cancelled, startedAt, finishedAt?, message}.

erase.description: {phase: backingUp|waiting|leaving|resetting|restarting|failed, backup, startedAt, deadline?, secondsLeft?, cancellable, message, outside}.

lastErase.description: {hadEdge, domainsRemoved, listingsClosed, leftEdge, problems, erasedAt}: counts only.

backupResponse.description: GET /api/backup: backups to an S3 bucket and the full erase.

sources.description: The catalogues searched, named so the screen can tell the reader where the rows came from. Sent even when `results` is empty, because "nothing matched on Artifact Hub" and "nothing matched" are different sentences and only the first one is true. Currently always ["Artifact Hub"].

results.description: Matching apps, at most 20, in the catalogue's own relevance order. A row the box cannot attribute to a publisher is dropped rather than returned: `source` is the only field on the row that tells the reader whose code they are about to run, and a result with nowhere to attribute it must not be shown as though this appliance vouched for it.

id.description: Stable identity for the row: the catalogue's own package id where it gives one, otherwise `<repository>/<package>`, which is unique within the catalogue.

name.description: Display name, falling back to the package name.

source.description: Who published it — the organisation where the catalogue names one, otherwise the repository. Required on every row; see the note on `results`.

summary.description: One-line description, or null. An empty or whitespace-only upstream value is sent as null rather than as an empty string, which is what the SPA's `nonEmptyString` would make of it anyway.

homepage.description: The package's own home page where it has one, otherwise its page on the catalogue, so every row stays clickable. Null only if neither can be built.

chart.description: Where the box can fetch the app from, for the Install button: the repository the catalogue names, the package and the version. Null when the catalogue names no `https://` or `oci://` repository; the row keeps its link and gets no button.

repo.description: `https://` for a chart repository, `oci://` for a registry, with no userinfo.

release.description: The app's name on this box. It names the Helm release, the namespace `losos-app-<release>` and the data folder `/home/<runAs>/data/apps/<release>`, so it never changes.

runAs.description: The user every pod runs as (uid 1000, 1001 or 1004), and the data domain its folders are in. Fixed at the first install. `kindashared` only while losos.sharingLocally is on.

values.description: The properties the owner changed from the chart's defaults, nested as in values.yaml. Applied after `valuesYaml`.

valuesYaml.description: The chart's values file as the owner edited it, or null to use the chart's own.

frontPort.description: The port nginx forwards from, LAN only, from losos.apps.ports. Kept across changes.

appPort.description: The port the app listens on, from its first Service, once the job has rendered it. Null for an app with no Service.

phase.description: A busy phase whose job unit is no longer active reads as failed.

message.description: Why it failed, in the box's words: the shaping's refusal or Helm's last line.

updatedAt.description: Unix seconds of the last phase change.

available.description: False on a box with no cluster of its own (LosOS Git native, or losos.apps.enable off). Then `reason` is noCluster and `apps` is empty.

sharedAvailable.description: Whether an app may run as shared: true only while the box shares its disk. Present when available.

kindasharedAvailable.description: Whether an app may run as kindashared: true only while the box shares with its local gateways (losos.sharingLocally). Present when available.

release.description: The name the box suggests, from the chart's name.

valuesYaml.description: The chart's values.yaml as published, for the text tab.

values.description: The same file as JSON, for the property form.

schema.description: The chart's values.schema.json, or null when it ships none.

edgeSource.description: Where an edge proxy was found: by DNS-SD on the local network (`_losos-edge._tcp`), or at losos.proxy.registrarUrl.

tunnel.description: `host:port` of this edge's tunnel server (QUIC on UDP, TLS on TCP as the fallback), where the box's tunnel would dial: the advert's `tunnel=` TXT record (or the registrar's host on port 2333 for an advert without one) for a LAN edge, losos.proxy.edgeTunnelEndpoint ($LOSOS_EDGE_TUNNEL) for the configured one. null when the box was given none, in which case the edge is found but never chosen as the path.

onNetwork.description: Found on the LAN, and both its registrar and its tunnel endpoint resolve only to addresses on a network this box is directly attached to (IPv4 ones private besides) (/proc/net/route, /proc/net/if_inet6). Only such an edge may manage the box.

official.description: This edge passed every gateway check on this box (backend/src/edge.rs, "gateways"): its TPM, certified by a maker in losos.proxy.gateways.tpmRoots, quoted a published image (losos.proxy.gateways.images) with its owner's signed passport and LosOS's payout addresses (losos.proxy.gateways.payouts), and nothing changed since it booted. Only such an edge may process P2P storage and compute trading; discovery and sharing do not depend on it.

name.description: The advertised DNS-SD instance name, or the configured URL's host.

url.description: Base URL of the edge's registrar API, no trailing slash. Listed only once its /health answered inside the probe budget.

gateway.description: What the gateway checks concluded, when the edge showed a passport (`GET <url>/passport?nonce=`). Absent for an edge with none, and on a box that ships no anchors.

state.description: `trusted`: every check passed. `refused`: not trusted now, asked again later. `disabled`: proved tampered; this box never trusts or tunnels through it again (/var/lib/losos/gateways.json).

owner.description: trusted: the owner's OpenPGP user id.

image.description: trusted: the published image it runs.

code.description: refused or disabled: the reason's code (malformed, passport, wrongUrl, nonceSignature, payoutChanged, noPayouts, unknownTpm, unknownImage, unknownBootEvent, forged, tainted, bootPath).

reason.description: refused or disabled: the reason in words.

since.description: disabled: Unix seconds it was disabled.

tier.description: Secondary for a gateway (it said so at GET /cluster/secondary, or it was found on the LAN and said nothing), tertiary for an official edge and for the configured edge unless it says it is a gateway.

cluster.description: The secondary cluster this gateway belongs to, as it named it (a DNS label). Absent for an official edge and for a gateway in no cluster, which counts as a cluster of its own named by its host.

officialCluster.description: The official cluster this official edge sits in: the official edges behind one load balancer, as the edge names it at GET /cluster/secondary (`officialCluster`). A ban may name the whole cluster. Absent for a gateway and for an edge that names none.

member.description: This gateway's name in its cluster.

url.description: The chosen edge's registrar API, as in `edges`.

tunnel.description: `host:port` the tunnel dials. Never null: an edge without one is not chosen.

cluster.description: The secondary cluster the path runs through; absent on a tertiary path.

officialCluster.description: The official cluster of a tertiary path, as in `edges`; absent otherwise. lososd writes it to /run/losos/edge-path.env as LOSOS_EDGE_PATH_OFFICIAL_CLUSTER.

member.description: The gateway's name in that cluster.

manage.description: Whether a company edge may manage LosOS Cloud, LosOS Git and the apps on this box (POST /api/edge/manage). Only the edge on the LAN the box uses can.

candidate.description: The edge in use that the owner could let manage the box, or null.

refused.description: Why no edge can: noLocalEdge when the box uses no edge found on the LAN, outsideNetwork when the edge in use resolves to addresses outside the box's own networks.

managedBy.description: The registrar URL management was switched on for, or null.

active.description: That edge is the one in use, so it manages the box now.

path.description: The edge this box uses, out of `edges` (handbook/docs/in-depth/edge-federation.md, "The box"): a gateway of the box's own secondary cluster (staying on the one in use while it answers, else the first by name), else an official edge (tertiary: the one in use while it answers, else the one a rendezvous hash of $LOSOS_APPLIANCE_ID weighs heaviest among those in reach, which spreads boxes across an official cluster's edges), else the configured edge, else null. Banned edges are dropped first (`leftBanned`), and a live custom domain holds the box to its edge (`held`). A box in no cluster settles in the one in reach with the most gateways. With losos.proxy.enable on, lososd writes it to /run/losos/edge-path.env (with LOSOS_EDGE_PATH_TIER and LOSOS_EDGE_PATH_CLUSTER) and restarts the tunnel and announce units when it changes; a move to another cluster also restarts losos-mesh-join and rke2-agent. null writes /run/losos/edge-none and stops them, so a box with no edge in reach runs no tunnel. The sharing gate (`reachable`) and the market gate (`official`) are the other two bits; this one says where the traffic goes.

official.description: At least one of `edges` is official. The one bit the market gate reads: while false, `GET /api/market` answers `{"available":false,"reason":"noOfficialEdge"}` and every `POST /api/market/*` is refused (HTTP 409, `{"error":"...","officialEdgeRequired":true}`), whatever edge the box is enrolled with. Sharing storage and joining the mesh are gated on `reachable` only.

localGateway.description: At least one of `edges` is a local gateway: its link from this box is secondary. The bit the kindashared gate reads: while false, an `apply` that turns losos.sharingLocally on is refused (HTTP 409, `localGatewayRequired`), and after losos.proxy.pauseSharingAfter seconds a box sharing locally pauses it (`localSharingPausedAt`).

localSharingPausedAt.description: Unix seconds when the box turned losos.sharingLocally off by itself because no local gateway answered; null when it did not, or once it turned it back on or the owner switched it.

reachable.description: At least one edge answered. The one bit the sharing gate reads: while false, `change --mode mesh` and an `apply` that turns losos.sharingMyStorage or losos.cluster.enable on are refused (HTTP 409, `{"error":"...","edgeRequired":true,"setting":"losos.<key>"}`). Settings already on are never refused, so a box whose edge went away keeps its configuration and can still change anything else.

edges.description: Every edge that answered, LAN first.

lanSearched.description: False when the LAN could not be browsed at all (systemd-resolved down, or it refused the browse): the LAN was not searched, as opposed to searched and empty.

configuredUrl.description: losos.proxy.registrarUrl as probed ($LOSOS_EDGE_URL), or null when none is set. Probed whether or not the master proxy is enabled.

checkedAt.description: Unix seconds of the scan this document describes; null before the first scan.

gateways.description: Its gateways that answered, by member name.

clusters.description: The secondary clusters in reach, by name.

cluster.description: The secondary cluster this box belongs to: the one the owner chose (POST /api/edge/cluster) or the one it settled in first. Kept while none of its gateways answers: the box never moves its own membership.

held.description: The registrar URL a live custom domain holds this box to ($LOSOS_STATE_DIR/edge-hold.env), or null. While held the box stays on that edge whether or not it answers, and POST /api/edge/cluster is refused with 409 `heldByDomain`. A ban on the edge or its official cluster breaks the hold: the box moves and the hold follows it to the new edge.

leftBanned.description: The banned edge this box moved off on the last choice, or null. Bans come from $LOSOS_EDGE_BANS_FILE, `{"edges":[<url>],"clusters":[<official cluster>]}`; a banned edge is never chosen, and a box on one moves to another edge of the same tier, the next official edge by load balancing for a tertiary path.

job.description: Identifies which rebuild this document describes, so a client can tell its own rebuild's outcome from a previous one's. Absent only when state is "idle", where there is no job.

stateFile.description: The persisted state at $LOSOS_STATE_DIR/state.json. Internal to the backend; not a wire response.

kind.description: The editor the admin UI's Advanced pane draws, decided from the option's Nix type by `classify` in nix/options-doc.nix. A type that file does not know is an evaluation error, so an option with a new type turns the eval check red rather than landing on the pane as an empty row; add it there AND in admin-ui/app/src/lib/option-value.ts.

pattern.description: str: the strMatching regex, when the type has one.

form.description: str: `path` for the secret-path options (a file on the box, typed as a string).

inner.description: nullable: the editor for the non-null value.

reason.description: opaque: the type's own description, shown on the read-only row.

available.description: False — with an empty `options` — when the box has no option document at $LOSOS_OPTIONS_FILE (an older build). A 200, not a 404, because the SPA latches a 404 as "route not served".

version.description: The document version (1). lososd refuses a document of another version rather than guess at its editor kinds.

options.description: Every `losos.*` option the box declares, from nix/options-doc.nix evaluated against the box's own configuration at build time and written to /etc/losos/options.json by modules/config-repo.nix. `losos.edge.*` is left out (declared for the VPS side; nothing on the appliance reads it).

group.description: The first path segment, or `general` for a top-level option.

nixType.description: nixpkgs' description of the type, for the row.

default.description: The declared default as JSON. A package is `{"package": "<name>"}`, anything JSON cannot carry is `{"nix": "<pretty-printed>"}`.

defaultText.description: The declaration's `defaultText`, or the default pretty-printed as Nix.

current.description: What the last rebuild merged, from the configuration the document was built against; same encoding as `default`.

danger.description: True for the options whose wrong value leaves the box unreachable, unbootable or locked out of the thing that would fix it (the `dangerous` prefixes in nix/options-doc.nix). The pane asks before changing one.

fixed.description: Who sets the value at normal priority, when someone does: `installer` for targetDrives, tpm.enable, bios and the two installer options, which modules/install-target.nix assigns, so a line in overrides.nix would make the next rebuild fail with conflicting definitions. Such an option is shown and refused.

readOnly.description: True when `fixed` is set or the editor is `opaque` (a package, a path, an attribute set — chosen by the flake, not typed into a form). An apply that assigns one is refused with 400.

set.description: The raw Nix literal overrides.nix currently assigns the option, or null when the file leaves it at its default. The legacy `cfd.enable` is joined onto `proxy.enable`, the option it became.

stray.description: Assignments in overrides.nix that name no declared option (a hand edit, or an option from another build). Listed so the pane can show they exist; an apply that carries one is refused.

excluded.description: Prefixes left out of the document, each with the reason.

enabled.description: Whether the box publishes /etc/nixos to a repository ($LOSOS_CONFIG_REPO or $LOSOS_CONFIG_REMOTE_URL set; modules/config-repo.nix sets the first when losos.configRepo.enable and losos.git.enable are both on). Off, the box still commits every change locally.

owner.description: The LosOS Git account the repository belongs to: the owner's (losos.configRepo.owner, default `notshared`). lososd creates it as a site administrator if missing; the owner signs in to it with LosOS Login.

name.description: losos.configRepo.name, default `losos-config`. Created private: /git/ is published through the master-proxy tunnel whenever the proxy is on.

url.description: The repository's page on this box, relative to the front vhost: `/git/<owner>/<name>`.

clone.description: The URL lososd fetches from and pushes to, without credentials. The owner clones the same repository through /git/ with a token of their own.

viaServer.description: False when $LOSOS_CONFIG_REMOTE_URL names the remote directly (the VM test's bare repository): no account and no repository are created, and no credentials are sent.

head.description: The branch head of /etc/nixos; null when nothing is committed (the next sync commits it).

subject.description: `Change hostName, cluster.enable`, `Reset sharingMyStorage`, `losos install`, or whatever a clone pushed.

state.description: How the last sync went. `ok`: in step, pushed, or a pushed commit taken (the detail says which). `unavailable`: LosOS Git is not up yet (no token, not answering) — the normal first minutes of a box. `refused`: a commit pushed from a clone failed the gates every Apply goes through (backend/src/overrides.rs validate_apply, then backend/src/options.rs check_body on its modules/overrides.nix); the box keeps its own and the detail says why. `diverged`: both sides moved; the box never force-pushes and never merges, so the owner resets the branch or pushes from a fresh clone. `waiting`: a pushed commit is held until the running rebuild finishes. `error`: anything else, with the sentence. `pending`: no sync has run yet. `off`: `enabled` is false.

syncedAt.description: RFC 3339, when the report was made.

remoteHead.description: The remote branch head after the sync, when there is one.

state.description: How the last look at the published branch went. `kept`: files other than modules/overrides.nix and modules/install-target.nix changed since the last follow (or since the install), so the box keeps its tree rather than overwrite them. `waiting`: a rebuild was running. `unavailable`: the source could not be fetched, and the nightly rebuild builds the current tree.

syncedAt.description: RFC 3339, when the report was made.

remoteHead.description: The published commit the last look fetched.

report.description: The outcome of the last ConfigUpdate, kept in config-upstream.json beside state.json.

upstream.description: Where /etc/nixos follows the published tree from. A follow is one commit on the box's branch whose tree is the published branch's newest tree with this box's modules/overrides.nix and modules/install-target.nix kept. nixos-upgrade.service asks for one (ConfigUpdate) before the nightly build.

edgeTier.description: Which kind of link (handbook/docs/in-depth/edge-federation.md, "Three tiers"). primary: edge to edge, the main cluster (gateways uplinked to an official edge). secondary: a box to a local gateway of its secondary cluster. tertiary: a box straight to an official edge, used only when no gateway of the box's own cluster answers. A box's own link is never primary.

state.description: `losos-ctl state --json` — current mode + sharing flag. stdout: stateResponse.

change.description: `losos-ctl change --mode <local|mesh>` — patch the losos.sharingMyStorage line of modules/overrides.nix in place (the same file `apply` writes whole), mark a rebuild as building, spawn a detached nixos-rebuild. Returns immediately. stdout: changeResponse. Non-zero exit + stderr on invalid mode.

status.description: `losos-ctl status --json` — rebuild progress, polled by the admin UI ~every 2s. stdout: statusResponse.

edge.description: `losos-ctl edge` — what lososd found when it last looked for an edge proxy. The daemon scans every 20 s: a DNS-SD browse for `_losos-edge._tcp` on the LAN through systemd-resolved's Varlink API (`io.systemd.Resolve.BrowseServices`, then `ResolveService` per instance; the edge advertises the service with a `url=` TXT record, losos.edge.lan.advertise), plus the configured registrar URL; every candidate's /health is probed and only the ones that answer are listed. stdout: edgeResponse.

settings.description: `losos-ctl settings --json` — the user-tunable losos.* options parsed from modules/overrides.nix. stdout: settingsResponse.

apply.description: `losos-ctl apply` — read Nix code (a full modules/overrides.nix body) from stdin, validate it references losos.*, is a module body, and carries a well-formed value for any of hostName, computeWindowStart and computeWindowEnd it sets, atomically overwrite modules/overrides.nix, mark a rebuild as building, start a supervised nixos-rebuild switch (systemd transient unit), and emit the job id on stdout. The admin UI generates the Nix code from the form and posts it. Non-zero exit + stderr on validation failure.

stdin.description: The full overrides.nix body the admin app generated.

factory-reset.description: `losos-ctl factory-reset` — soft factory reset: atomically restore modules/overrides.nix to the committed default body, reset the persisted state to defaultState (Local, sharing off), mark a rebuild as building, start a supervised nixos-rebuild, and emit the job id. Non-destructive: it only touches lososd's own state + overrides.nix. The destructive tier (wipe disks + reinstall) is the installer ISO, which auto-runs `losos-install` as root's login shell.

grow.description: `losos-ctl grow` — extend /persist into the volume group's unallocated extents, online. Three steps in a fixed order: lvextend, then cryptsetup resize, then resize2fs. The order is load-bearing and the failure is silent — resize2fs asks the LUKS mapping for its size, so running it before cryptsetup resize reads the pre-grow size, prints "Nothing to do!" and exits 0. Nothing is unmounted and no rebuild is triggered. The space comes from the margin modules/disko.nix leaves at install time (losos.storage.fillPercent, default 90); when that is exhausted, add a disk with pvcreate + vgextend and run this again. Errors when the volume group has no free extents, rather than succeeding with an empty plan.

set-password.description: `losos-ctl set-password [--user <name>]` — replace the owner's LosOS Login password, read from **stdin**. Stdin and not a flag because /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable and nothing in modules/ sets hidepid, so `--password <value>` would publish the box's admin credentials to every process on it. Exactly one trailing newline is stripped, nothing else: a password may end in a space. The password goes to the people file (backend/src/people.rs, argon2id) and, when LosOS Git keeps the owner's account, to Forgejo's admin API over loopback, never an argv. Rejected server-side, before any effect: a password under 12 characters, without a lower-case letter, an upper-case letter, a digit and a symbol (Unicode-aware: Ž and ß count as letters; a symbol is anything that is neither a letter, a digit nor whitespace), over 256 bytes, or containing a control character, and a user name that is not [A-Za-z0-9._@-] or that starts with '-'. Non-zero exit and stderr on any of those.

stdin.description: The new password. One trailing newline is stripped.

recovery.description: `losos-ctl recovery` — print the appliance recovery code, minting one on first use. Idempotent: every later call returns the same code and writes nothing. There is deliberately no rotate subcommand. NOTE: nothing consumes this code. It was conceived as proof that a re-imaged box is the same box, but that lockout is already prevented by /cluster/join in edge/registrar, which deletes the caller's stale Node object and node-password Secret before handing back a mesh token and proves identity with the proxy token the box already has. There is no `recovery` map in registry.json and no /recover route, and building one would be a different feature — self-service re-issue of the proxy token over an unauthenticated route — which has not been agreed. See the second section of backend/src/recovery.rs. Clients must not imply the code recovers anything. Non-zero exit + stderr when the code file exists but cannot be read — minting over an unreadable file would destroy a code the owner still holds, so that case fails loudly instead.

install.description: `losos-ctl install [flags]` — the losos auto-installer (was losos-install.sh). Detects fixed disks, merges them into one LVM volume group via disko, runs nixos-install, and lays the flake at /persist/etc/nixos. Flags: --tpm, --drives A,/dev/b,..., --no-install, --disko-script PATH, --emit-target FILE. Drives auto-detection uses `lsblk --json`. Non-zero exit + stderr on failure (no candidate disks, disko/nixos-install failure).

options.description: `losos-ctl options` — print every losos.* option this box declares (from /etc/losos/options.json, written at build time by modules/config-repo.nix from nix/options-doc.nix), with its editor kind, default, current value and what overrides.nix sets. The document the admin UI's Advanced pane is drawn from, and the second gate `apply` goes through: a body that assigns an undeclared or read-only option, or a literal of the wrong kind, is refused by name.

config.description: `losos-ctl config [--sync]` — the box's configuration repository: /etc/nixos is a git repository (made by the installer), every apply, change and factory-reset commits there with a message naming the settings, and lososd keeps it in step with the owner's private repository on LosOS Git every half minute (backend/src/config_repo.rs). With --sync, one sync now: push what the box has, or take a commit pushed from a clone — after its modules/overrides.nix passes the two apply gates — and rebuild. The repository holds no secrets: the LUKS keyfile is under /etc/keys and every token under /var/secrets.

sync.description: --sync: sync with LosOS Git now instead of waiting for the next run.

http.note: lososd also serves a Bearer-authed JSON API on 127.0.0.1:$LOSOS_ADMIN_PORT (default 8082); Nginx proxies /api/* to it for the admin UI. Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The scheme is case-insensitive per RFC 7235, and lososd compares the token in constant time. The token lives at $LOSOS_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE (default /var/secrets/losos-admin-token), minted on first start as 64 lowercase hex characters, mode 0600. lososd discards and re-mints any file that does not hold exactly that, so a truncated or hand-edited token never becomes the shared secret. Responses are the same documents as the facade wire; errors are `{"error": "..."}` with the matching HTTP status. A 500 carries a fixed message and lososd logs the detail to the journal, because the context chain names filesystem paths.

POST /api/apply.note: Two gates, in order: validate_apply (backend/src/overrides.rs: a module body naming losos.* options, a hostName that will not brick the box, HH:MM windows), then — on a box carrying /etc/losos/options.json — check_body (backend/src/options.rs): every `losos.<key> = <literal>;` line must name a declared, writable option and fit its editor kind, and no value may carry `${`. A refusal is 400 with a sentence naming the key. The body then replaces overrides.nix, is committed to /etc/nixos with a message naming the changed settings, and a rebuild is queued.

GET /api/storage.note: Read-only: the size of /persist, how much of it is in use, and the reserve POST /api/grow would claim (df and vgs). The Storage pane draws its meter and disables Use reserve from it, so a reload or a second browser sees a claimed reserve as claimed. A reading the box cannot take is null. HTTP-only, like /api/apps/search: it backs a settings screen.

GET /api/me.out: {"name": "..."|null, "displayName": "..."|null, "groups": ["..."], "admin": bool, "spareKey": bool, "sections": ["..."], "standalone": bool, "edge": bool, "locked": ["twoFactor"|"password"], "shared": ["mail", "chat", "contacts"], "role": "owner"|"admin"|"moderator"|"member"|"guest", "roleName": "..."|null, "reports": n (moderators only)}
GET /api/me.note: Who is calling (backend/src/http.rs, get_me). A person signed in at the box's sign-in page (Authelia at /auth/) arrives as the Remote-User nginx sets from Authelia's answer; lososd looks them up in the people file it writes (backend/src/people.rs) and answers with their name, groups and the sections of backend/sections.json those groups open. `standalone` is true when this box signs people in itself (LOSOS_IDENTITY=authelia), which is when the Users pane is shown. The spare key answers with name null, admin true and spareKey true. The admin pages show the panes `sections` names and hide the rest. 401 signed out; 403 with noAccount:true for a Remote-User the people file does not hold (removed since they signed in). A company edge the owner lets manage the box (POST /api/edge/manage) answers with edge true, name null, admin false and the sections it may use. `locked` lists what a rule of LosOS Login holds the person to their own account for (backend/src/login.rs); while it is not empty, `sections` is ["account"], `admin` is false, and every other route but the signed-in ones answers 403 with locked:true. `shared` (a person's only) names the apps that run as the `shared` user and are live on this box now, which is only while it shares its storage: the page draws their entries only when they are named here. `role` is the caller's role, a layer over their groups (backend/src/roles.rs), and `roleName` the name of a role of the box's own when they hold one. `reports` counts the open reports for anyone who can open the Moderation pane.

GET /api/chat.note: LosOS Chat (backend/src/chat.rs, modules/chat.nix): whether the homeserver answers, and the part after the colon in every user ID. 404 {"error"} when chat is not live on this box: it is off, or the box does not both share its storage and belong to a mesh.

GET /api/chat/people.note: Everyone in LosOS Login who may chat, so the page can offer them before they have ever signed in: the homeserver's user directory lists only people who share a room. Makes each one's account through the application service on first sight, keeping the display name in step; a disabled person or one a rule of LosOS Login holds is left out. 403 for the spare key and the edge; 503 while the homeserver starts; 404 when chat is not live.

GET /api/contacts/suggest.note: People pickers (Mail's To and Cc, starting a chat, the Contacts book's On this box, mesh sharing, @-mentions): ?q=&want=any|email|matrix|mesh|box&limit=8 (1 to 50). The caller's contacts, from LosOS Cloud's address books (GET /cloud/api/contacts/suggest as the caller, backend/src/cloud/contacts.rs, which also keeps the book itself under /cloud/api/contacts/), and the people on this box, best match first, accents ignored. A box person who is a contact by Matrix ID shows once, as the contact; want=mesh offers contacts only; want=box offers everyone on this box but the caller, contacts or not, and no contacts. Box people carry a matrixId only where chat runs and an address only where mail does; without LosOS Cloud there are no contacts. 403 for the spare key and the edge.

POST /api/chat/session.in: {"device": "<device ID the page had>" (optional), "deviceName": "..." (optional, at most 64 characters)}
POST /api/chat/session.note: Sign a chat device in for the person LosOS Login signed in. The first call makes their account, @<name>:<serverName>, through the application service lososd is; nobody has a Matrix password. Keeps their display name in step with LosOS Login. A `device` the page had keeps that device (and its end-to-end keys); a malformed one is ignored. 403 for the spare key, the edge, and a person a rule of LosOS Login holds; 503 while the homeserver starts; 404 when chat is not live. Cache-Control no-store. Every request with the token then passes GET /internal/chat/authz.

GET /internal/chat/authz.out: empty: 200 go on, 401 sign in with LosOS Login, 403 not yours, 404 chat not live, 503 not answering
GET /internal/chat/authz.note: Asked by nginx alone (an internal location in modules/chat.nix) before every request to the homeserver's client and media APIs, with the request's Cookie, Authorization, X-Original-URL, X-Original-Method and X-Forwarded-For. lososd asks LosOS Login about the cookie, wants the person still in the people file and not held, and a Matrix token, when there is one, of that same person (asked of the homeserver, remembered by its SHA-256 for five minutes). A token the homeserver does not know goes on, so the homeserver answers M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN itself.

GET /api/people.out: {"standalone": bool, "you": "..."|null, "sections": ["..."], "rules": {"twoFactor": bool, "passwordDays": n}, "people": [{"name": "...", "displayName": "...", "email": "...", "groups": ["..."], "disabled": bool, "twoFactor": bool, "passwordSetAt": seconds, "locked": ["twoFactor"|"password"], "role": "...", "roleName": "..."|null, "muted": hold|null, "suspended": hold|null}], "roles": [{"id": "...", "name": "...", "sections": ["..."]}]}
GET /api/people.note: Everyone in the people file (backend/src/people.rs), never a password hash, for the Users pane. `you` is the caller's name, null for the spare key. `sections` are the parts of backend/sections.json a person can be given one by one. On a box that does not sign people in itself `standalone` is false and `people` is empty. Administrators only. `roles` are the box's own roles (roles.json); a hold is {at, by, until: seconds|null, reason}.

POST /api/people.note: Add someone who may sign in at /auth/. `groups` are losos-admins, losos-viewers or losos-<section>; anything else is a 400, as are a bad name or a short password. `email` defaults to <name>@<hostname>.local. 409 for a name already taken, or with standalone:false on a box that does not sign people in itself. Administrators only.

POST /api/people/access.note: Replace someone's access groups (the same set as POST /api/people). Other groups, such as losos-owner, stay. 404 for nobody by that name; 409 for the caller's own account, the owner's, or a change that would leave no administrator. Administrators only. A role goes out as its groups: losos-admins; losos-moderation (the moderator); losos-guests with losos-account; losos-role-<id> for a role of the box's own, which lososd fills in with that role's sections; or losos-<section> one by one for a member. Moderation is never given as a part on its own.

POST /api/people/password.note: Set a new password for someone who forgot theirs. 409 for the owner, who changes their own through POST /api/set-password so their LosOS Git password follows. Administrators only.

POST /api/people/remove.note: Take someone out of the people file: their next request is a 403 with noAccount:true and they cannot sign in again. Their LosOS Cloud and LosOS Git accounts and files stay. 404 for nobody by that name; 409 for the caller, the owner, or the last administrator. Administrators only.

POST /api/people/rules.note: LosOS Login's two rules (backend/src/login.rs): everyone needs an authenticator app or a passkey, and a password runs out passwordDays after it was set (0 never). Someone a rule holds reaches only their own account, and Authelia keeps them out of LosOS Cloud and LosOS Git, until they comply. 409 with needsOwnFactor:true when a person turns twoFactor on without a second factor of their own. Administrators only.

POST /api/people/two-factor/reset.note: Remove someone's authenticator app and passkeys from LosOS Login, for a lost phone or key. 404 for nobody by that name. Administrators only.

POST /api/roles.note: Save a role of the box's own in /var/lib/losos/roles.json (backend/src/roles.rs): a name of 1 to 40 characters and the sections it opens. At most 16; a name taken twice is a 409. Everyone holding it gets the new sections at once. Administrators only.

POST /api/roles/remove.note: Remove a role of the box's own. Whoever held it becomes a member with their own account and nothing more. Administrators only.

POST /api/reports.note: Report something to the box's moderators (backend/src/moderation.rs). `ref` names the thing in its app (a mail id, <room ID>/<event ID> in chat, picture or banner) and is never its content. A report about a child keeps no note. The same report twice is one report; 20 open from one person is a 429. Anyone signed in, guests too.

GET /api/moderation.out: {"standalone": bool, "you": "..."|null, "admin": bool, "hides": ["mail", "chat" (while chat is live), "profile"], "reports": [{"id", "at", "by", "app", "about", "ref", "reason", "note", "state": "open"|"hidden"|"dismissed"|"resolved", "handledBy", "handledAt"}], "people": [profile + {"role", "roleName", "muted": hold|null, "suspended": hold|null, "disabled": bool, "actionable": bool}], "log": [{"at", "by", "action", "about", "detail"}]}
GET /api/moderation.note: The Moderation pane: the queue (open first, child reports first, newest first), everyone with what the caller may do to them, and the latest lines of /var/lib/losos/moderation.log. `hides` are the apps the queue can hide a thing in. Moderators and administrators; viewers do not read it.

POST /api/moderation/reports/{id}.out: the report as it now stands: {"id", ..., "state", "handledBy", "handledAt"}
POST /api/moderation/reports/{id}.note: Act on a report. hide moves a mail into the reporter's Quarantine mailbox (no page lists it and lososd refuses to open it), redacts a chat message as its sender (a chat report's ref is <room ID>/<event ID>), or takes a profile picture or banner down; release lets held mail go; a report about a child can only be hidden, or resolved where the box cannot hide it, never dismissed or released. 409 for a closed report. Moderators and administrators.

POST /api/moderation/mute.note: Stop someone sending mail, writing in chat and changing their profile (the `speech` routes of backend/sections.json answer 403 with muted, and /internal/chat/authz refuses what they would say in a room) for `minutes`, or until unmuted when null. Administrators may hold anyone but the owner; moderators members and guests; nobody themselves. Moderators and administrators.

POST /api/moderation/unmute.note: Lift a mute. Moderators and administrators.

POST /api/moderation/suspend.note: Keep someone out: their people-file record is disabled, so LosOS Login refuses their next request and their next sign-in, and lososd answers 403 with suspended. A timed suspension lifts itself. Same rank rules as mute. Moderators and administrators.

POST /api/moderation/unsuspend.note: Let someone back in. Moderators and administrators.

GET /api/account.note: The caller's own account on LosOS Login, for Your account. Section account; a person a rule holds reaches it whatever their sections. 409 for the spare key, which has no account, and on a box that does not sign people in itself.

POST /api/account.note: The caller's own name (1 to 100 characters, one line) and email address. LosOS Cloud and LosOS Git get them too, in the background (backend/src/app_names.rs). 400 with the reason otherwise. Section account.

POST /api/account/code.note: The one-time code LosOS Login last made for the caller, which it asks for before they add or remove an authenticator app or a passkey. The box sends no email, so the code is read from Authelia's notification file, behind the caller's password. 403 with wrongPassword:true, 404 with noCode:true. Section account.

POST /api/devices/cloud.note: A LosOS Cloud app password of one computer's own, for `losos cloud setup` (backend/src/devices.rs). lososd checks the owner's password against the people file first, throttled per address like the spare key, then asks LosOS Cloud over its socket (/run/losos-cloud/http.sock) to mint one for the owner, never an argv. `device` (1-48 letters, digits, spaces, dots, dashes, underscores) names the app password `LosOS on <device>` in the owner's devices list. 403 with wrongPassword:true on a wrong password (not 401: the caller's token is good); 429 when the address has tried too many; 503 when LosOS Cloud cannot be asked; 400 for a body of the wrong shape. HTTP-only; reached by the terminal client as a sealed call.

POST /api/devices/git.note: A LosOS Git access token of one computer's own, for `losos git setup` (backend/src/devices.rs). lososd checks the password against the owner's LosOS Login account, then asks LosOS Git with its admin token over loopback for a token named `LosOS on <device>` on the owner's account, replacing one of the same name, with scopes write:repository and read:user. 403 with wrongPassword:true on a wrong password; 409 with gitOff:true when LosOS Git is off on this box; 503 when it cannot be asked. HTTP-only; reached by the terminal client as a sealed call.

POST /api/devices/backups.note: Both credentials a computer's backups need, for LosOS Desktop's `losos-backup sign-in box` (backend/src/losos.rs cmd_device_backups). The caller is a person: LosOS Login's device code sign-in as the client `losos-backups` (losos_access::BACKUPS_CLIENT_ID), whose token reaches this route and nothing else, or a person signed in in the browser. No password: LosOS Login asked for it, the second factor and consent. The person's own accounts (the owner's are notshared and the configuration repository's owner): a LosOS Cloud app password and a LosOS Git token named `LosOS on <device>`, each replacing one of that name, and a person new to LosOS Cloud is made there first. `git` is null with gitOff on a box without LosOS Git; an app that could not make one leaves its key null and says why in `problems`. 503 when neither could; 403 with locked:true for an account LosOS Login holds to its rules; 400 for a body of the wrong shape or a bad device name. Section signed-in. HTTP-only.

POST /api/devices/directory.note: Joins a LosOS Desktop computer to this box (backend/src/directory.rs), for its `losos-login-bridge join`. Admin only: the administrator's LosOS Login session or the spare key. The answer carries the computer's token, the only time it exists outside the computer; only its SHA-256 is kept, in directory.json in the state directory. Joining again under the same `device` replaces the old token. 400 for a bad device name, 409 when 256 computers are joined. HTTP-only.

GET /api/devices/directory.note: The joined LosOS Desktop computers, without tokens. Admin only. HTTP-only.

DELETE /api/devices/directory/{id}.note: Takes a joined computer out: its token stops at once. The company accounts already on it stay and log in offline. Admin only; 404 for an unknown id. HTTP-only.

GET /api/directory/people.note: The people list a joined LosOS Desktop computer reads on a timer, to lock the accounts this box removed or disabled. The caller is the computer's `Authorization: Bearer losos_dir_...` token, which reaches this route and nothing else and is nobody everywhere else (403), or an administrator. No password hash or second factor leaves the box. 409 when LosOS Login does not run here. HTTP-only.

POST /api/directory/jobs/claim.note: A joined LosOS Desktop computer asks for its next Mesh CI job (`runs-on: [losos-desktop, <computer>]`, backend/src/ci/workflow.rs `desktop_job`): waits up to 15 s (inside a client's 20 s read timeout), relayed to losos-ci as the computer its `losos_dir_` token names. The steps are fixed actions (`losos/desktop-*`) with their `with:` filled in on the box. 204 when there is nothing, or no Mesh CI on this box. Only a directory token; 403 for anyone else. HTTP-only.

POST /api/directory/jobs/report.note: The computer's log and result for a job it took; `stop` says the run was cancelled. A computer reports only on its own running jobs (403 otherwise). Only a directory token. HTTP-only.

GET /api/apps/search.in: query string: q=<search term>, 2-128 characters, no control characters
GET /api/apps/search.note: Searches a public app catalogue from the box. The admin pages are served under `connect-src 'self'`, so the browser cannot reach a catalogue itself — lososd is the only thing here with an outbound path. HTTP-only, with no D-Bus method and no facade subcommand, following `POST /api/setup/claim`: the facade exists to control this appliance, and a CLI for a settings screen's search field would be surface with no caller. A bad or missing `q` is 400 with the reason, deliberately NOT 404 — the SPA latches a 404 as "this box does not serve the route" and stops asking for the rest of the session. A search that could not be made (no route off the box, the catalogue down, a body that is not JSON) is 500, which the screen shows as retryable.

GET /api/cloud/text.in: query string: q=<search>, 1-128 characters with at least one letter or digit, no control characters; limit=1-20 (default 8)
GET /api/cloud/text.note: Text inside the owner's files in LosOS Cloud (backend/src/textsearch/, modules/search.nix). lososd relays to the socket-activated `losos-search cloud` on /run/losos-search/cloud.sock, which searches an SQLite FTS5 index the `losos-search-index` timer keeps current; every word must appear, each as a word prefix, accents ignored. `path` is from the owner's root without a leading slash; `snippet` alternates plain and matched runs, starting with a plain one. `partial` is true until the first pass over the files has finished. `off` is losos.search.enable = false; `notUp` is nothing listening on the socket. A bad `q` is 400, deliberately NOT 404, which the SPA latches. HTTP-only, following /api/apps/search.

GET /api/git/text.in: query string: q and limit as GET /api/cloud/text
GET /api/git/text.note: Lines on the default branch of every LosOS Git repository that contain every word, ignoring case (`git grep -F -i` per repository, as the losos-git user, under `losos-search git` on /run/losos-search/git.sock). Wikis are left out, at most two lines per file, and the search answers with what it found after four seconds. `noGit` is a box without losos.git.enable, or with losos.search.enable off. Same 400 and HTTP-only rules as GET /api/cloud/text.

GET /api/apps.note: The apps installed from the search (backend/src/apps.rs, records in /var/lib/losos/apps/<release>/app.json, mode 0600). Not-offered is 200 with available:false, deliberately NOT 404, which the SPA latches. HTTP-only, following /api/apps/search.

GET /api/apps/chart.in: query string: repo=<https:// or oci:// URL>&name=<chart>&version=<version>
GET /api/apps/chart.note: The chart's values and schema for the install dialog. lososd pulls the chart with `helm pull` into a temporary directory, without holding its lock. 400 for a repository the box would not fetch from, 409 on a box with no cluster, 500 when the pull fails.

POST /api/apps/install.note: Install, or change an app already installed under the same name, as a `losos-app-<release>` transient unit (modules/apps.nix). Answers with the record in phase installing; the job runs `helm upgrade --install` with the losos-shape post-renderer and writes the outcome back. 409 when shared is asked for while the box does not share its disk, when the name holds another chart or the other user, or while a job for it is running. 400 for a bad name, chart or values (64 KiB of JSON, 256 KiB of YAML). Audited.

POST /api/apps/remove.note: Uninstall, in a `losos-app-<release>` unit. Answers with the record in phase removing; the job deletes it once Helm is done. The app's folders under /home/<runAs>/data/apps/<release> stay. 409 while a job for it is running, 400 for an unknown name. Audited.

GET /api/market.note: The optional storage/compute market, relayed to the edge's registrar (backend/src/market.rs). The pages cannot call the edge themselves under `connect-src 'self'`, and the registrar wants the appliance's proxy token, which the browser must not hold. HTTP-only, following /api/apps/search. Not-offered is 200 with available:false, deliberately NOT 404, which the SPA latches.

POST /api/market/onboard.note: Start or resume Stripe Connect onboarding. Audited. The body is ignored: lososd itself sends the registrar this box's UUID, derived one-way from the recovery code (backend/src/boxid.rs, so the code is never sent), and the edge writes it onto the Stripe account as metadata.

POST /api/market/listings.note: List what this box already shares on the mesh. 409 with the registrar's reason when it is not sharing it, or has not finished onboarding. Audited.

POST /api/market/listings/close.note: Stop selling a listing. Orders already paid keep their units. Audited.

POST /api/market/orders.note: Buy units. Returns a Stripe Checkout URL for the page to open. Audited. Owner-actionable refusals are 400/409 carrying the registrar's own sentence.

POST /api/market/release.note: Pay this box now for its sales whose slots are over, instead of waiting for the edge to do it a day after each slot ends (registrar POST /market/sales/release). The body is ignored. The reply adds held, ready, paying and next_at, in minor units and Unix seconds, as the account's payouts. 409 while nothing is ready: every sale's slot still runs, or nothing is held. Audited.

POST /api/market/fees/pay.note: Count a USDC transfer from this box's EVM payout address to the edge's treasury against the platform fees owed on coin sales (registrar POST /market/fees/pay). The reply adds paid, credited and owed, in cents. The edge reads the receipt itself, waits for its confirmations (409 until then), counts a transaction once and never more than is owed; a surplus is kept. Solana is refused with 400. Audited.

POST /api/market/llm/models.note: AI models run on memory boxes lend, paid per token through the edge (registrar POST /market/llm/models, edge/registrar/src/server/llm.rs), relayed like the market. A view and not audited: an edge that runs no models, a box not cleared for the market or no official edge in reach is 200 with available:false. Prices are USDC base units per million tokens and amounts are base units, all as decimal text, except billedE6 (millionths of a base unit) and a wallet's balance, asked and notBefore (numbers). The edge picks its first network when none is named.

POST /api/market/taps.in: {"model": "[a-z0-9-]{1,64}", "network"?: "<network key>", "spendPerHour": <USDC base units, 10000 to 100000000, number or decimal text>}
POST /api/market/taps.note: Quote a meter for one model (registrar POST /market/taps): one tap per lending box, which the owner's wallet opens in the escrow (LososEscrow.openTaps, or the losos-escrow program's open_tap) before openBefore, then confirms. 409 while the model already runs for this box, 503 with the reason while too few boxes lend memory for it. Audited.

POST /api/market/taps/confirm.note: `wallet` opened the meter's taps (registrar POST /market/taps/confirm): the edge reads each one back from the chain, where the escrow keeps it under that wallet, which can take 20 s, and opens the meter when all are as quoted. Audited.

POST /api/market/taps/stop.note: Stop a meter (registrar POST /market/taps/stop). The edge closes its taps and settles them one last time; the wallet signs nothing. `wallet` is the wallet that began opening a quoted meter's taps and failed partway: the edge reads them back from the chain, closes the ones it holds and keeps the wallet's balance in view. Audited.

POST /api/market/llm/chat.in: {"meter": "mtr_<hex>", "messages": [{"role": "system|user|assistant", "content"}] (1 to 256, 256 KiB of content in all), "maxTokens"?: <1 to the model's context>, "temperature"?: <0 to 2>, "topP"?: <0 to 1>, "stop"?: string | [string] (at most 4, each 1 to 64 bytes)}
POST /api/market/llm/chat.note: One request to a running model, billed per token on the meter (registrar POST /market/llm/chat). An answer can take up to 16 minutes; lososd waits 17, off its HTTP worker and without its state lock. The boxes running the model can read the prompt and the answer. Refusals keep the edge's sentence: 402 when the balance or the hourly limit cannot cover the request, 429 while another request runs on the meter, 503 while the model loads or a box restarts, 409 when the meter is not open. A failed answer is not billed. Audited when the answer is back.

GET /api/builder.note: The widget builder (backend/src/builder.rs): a language model on this box, Ollama on loopback (modules/builder.nix, losos.builder.*), writes a widget or an app from the owner's description. Nothing leaves the box and nothing is charged. reason is off when the box runs no builder, starting while Ollama does not answer, downloading until it has the model. buildSummary is {"id", "kind": "widget|app", "status": "running|done|failed|stopped", "prompt", "revision", "created_at", "finished_at", "lines", "fixing", "fault", "has_source"}, newest first, the last ten since lososd started. A 200 in every case.

POST /api/builder/builds.in: {"prompt": "1-2000 characters", "kind"?: "widget|app" (widget when left out), "base"?: [{"name", "content"}] (the widget to change, under the same limits as a saved one and at most 10 KiB together; a plain string is read as its index.html) | "<JSX>" (the app to change, at most 64 KiB), "lang"?: "en|sk|de"}
POST /api/builder/builds.note: Start a build on a thread of its own and answer at once with it running. 400 with a sentence for a request the builder will not act on, 409 while a build is running or the box runs no builder. build is {"id", "kind": "widget|app", "status": "running|done|failed|stopped", "prompt", "revision", "created_at", "finished_at", "lines", "fixing", "fault": null|"noWidget|noApp|unusable|upstream|memory", "at_limit", "files": [{"name", "content"}]|null, "name": string|null, "code": string|null, "problems": [string], "notes": string|null, "steps": [step], "trial": {"id", "code"}|null}. For an app, files is [{"name": "app.jsx", "content"}], name is the name the model gave it, code is the script the app frame runs when the source compiles (while the build runs, the version it is on), and problems are the mistakes the box and the try still find, as sentences. A build is a loop: the model writes, the box checks, an app is tried in the page, and the model fixes what was found, up to three times for an app and once for a widget; the best answer is kept. step is {"kind": "write|check|try|fix", "running", "problems": [string], "shown": [string] (a try: what the app showed, a line per element), "skipped" (a try no page answered), "started_at"}. trial is the app the build asks the page to try now; see POST /api/builder/builds/{id}/tried. Audited.

GET /api/builder/builds/{id}.note: One build. lines counts the answer so far while it runs. files is the widget once it is done, index.html first, or the app as app.jsx; at_limit says the answer ran into its length limit. 404 for a build lososd does not know, which is every build after it restarts. The page puts a widget in the editor and saves it only when the owner says so, through POST /api/look/widgets, so it runs in /widget-frame/ like any widget written by hand; an app goes to the app editor and is saved through POST /api/user-apps.

POST /api/builder/builds/{id}/tried.note: What the page found when it tried the app the build asked it to: the preview frame filled every field, pressed the first button and said what the app showed, the button's words, which collections changed, and, when none did, which choices it changed before pressing again and what changed then, and what it threw on start and on the press. Each list is cut to 40 lines of 200 characters. No app code runs on the box, so this is the only way a build sees an app run; a build that hears nothing in 30 seconds (LOSOS_BUILDER_TRY_SECS) carries on untried. 404 for a build lososd does not know, 409 when it is not waiting for that trial or already has its report. Audited.

DELETE /api/builder/builds/{id}.note: Stop a running build; its status becomes stopped and the model's answer is dropped. A build that has finished is returned as it is. 404 for one lososd does not know. Audited.

GET /api/user-apps.note: The owner's own apps (backend/src/user_apps.rs), without their code, oldest first, from /var/lib/losos/user-apps.json. Anyone signed in may list and open them; making, changing and deleting one is the apps section's (sections.json). Times are Unix seconds.

POST /api/user-apps.in: {"id"?: "u<n>" (a new version of that app), "name": "1-60 characters", "summary"?: string|null (at most 600), "prompt"?: string|null, "source": "<JSX>" (at most 64 KiB)}
POST /api/user-apps.note: Add an app, or replace the one id names, keeping its data. The source is one React component in JSX (backend/src/jsx.rs): parsed, checked for components, hooks and globals that do not exist in the app frame, and compiled to a plain script, once, on the box. Source that does not compile is refused with 400 and the first mistake as a sentence; source that compiles is kept even when the checks still find something, which is returned in problems. 404 for an id the box does not have, 409 at 24 apps. userApp is {"id", "name", "summary", "prompt", "source", "code", "createdAt", "updatedAt"}. Audited.

POST /api/user-apps/check.note: Compile and check source the way a save would, keeping nothing: the app editor's preview and its list of mistakes. code is null when the source does not compile.

GET /api/user-apps/{id}.note: One app with its source and the compiled script the page hands the app frame (/app-frame/, sandbox="allow-scripts allow-forms", nginx's own CSP arm). 404 for an id the box does not have.

DELETE /api/user-apps/{id}.note: Delete an app and everything kept in it. Audited.

GET /api/user-apps/{id}/data.note: What the app keeps (useCollection and useStored in the app frame), from /var/lib/losos/user-apps/<id>.json. 404 for an app the box does not have.

POST /api/user-apps/{id}/data.note: One write from the app, relayed by the page. The box gives an added entry its id and createdAt (milliseconds) and never lets an update change an id. Names are letters, digits, - and _, up to 40 characters, at most 32 collections and keys; one entry is at most 32 KiB and everything an app keeps at most 2 MiB, past which the write is refused with 400 and a sentence. 404 for an app or an entry the box does not have.

GET /api/vms.note: Virtual machines on the mesh, sold per replica through the market (edge/registrar/src/vms.rs). Offered only while this box shares its disk: otherwise available:false with reason notSharing, and every /api/vms action below is refused with 409 before the edge is asked. A 200 in every not-offered case, deliberately NOT 404.

POST /api/vms/orders.in: {"listing_id": "...", "quantity": <replicas, 1-10>, "image": "<catalogue id or upl_...>", "name": "<1-40 printable characters>", "user_data": "<cloud-init, optional, at most 16 KiB>"}
POST /api/vms/orders.note: Order replicas of a machine. Returns the Stripe Checkout URL. The fee is half the total, whatever the edge's market fee. Audited.

POST /api/vms/listings.note: Offer to host machines on this box. 409 with the registrar's reason unless the box is enrolled in the mesh and hosts machines. Audited.

POST /api/vms/listings/close.note: Stop offering machines. Running machines keep their month. Audited.

PUT /api/vms/images.in: query string name=<1-40 printable characters>&efi=1 (optional); the body is the QCOW2 file
PUT /api/vms/images.note: Upload an image of this box's own. lososd takes a single-use ticket from the edge, then streams the body to it with curl (the ticket in a temporary config file, not in argv) without holding its lock; nginx passes the body unbuffered. The edge's refusal comes back with its status: 413 over the size limit, 415 not a QCOW2, 409 too many images, 408 when the transfer stalls; 502 when the edge cannot be reached. Audited.

POST /api/vms/images/remove.note: Delete one of this box's images from the edge. Audited.

GET /api/lab/hello.note: LosOS Lab's libvirt helper (`losos-registrar lab`, losos.lab.libvirt.enable), relayed to its GET /lab/v1/hello with the admin token (backend/src/lab.rs). Off or not running is 200 with available:false and a reason, deliberately NOT 404.

POST /api/lab/guests.note: Start one Lab guest as a transient libvirt domain. Relayed as is; the helper checks every field and answers 201, 400, 409 (full), 502 (libvirt refused) or 503 (no libvirt, or an image missing). 503 here too when no helper runs. The guest's console and NICs are WebSockets at /api/lab/ws/<guest>/console and /api/lab/ws/<guest>/nic/<n>, which nginx proxies to the helper directly; they authenticate with `ticket.<ticket>` as a WebSocket subprotocol. Audited.

POST /api/lab/virt-ticket.note: A single-use ticket, good for 30 seconds, for the WebSocket at /api/lab/virt, which nginx proxies straight to the helper's GET /lab/v1/virt: a byte relay to libvirt's unix socket with no parsing, sent `ticket.<ticket>` as a subprotocol beside `losos-lab`. Whoever holds the socket has libvirt at the helper's uid (root-equivalent under qemu:///system), hence the admin token here. 503 when no helper runs or the URI has no local socket. Audited.

GET /api/domains.note: This box's custom domains on an official edge, relayed to the registrar's POST /domains/list like the market (backend/src/market.rs `Op::Domains`). Asked only of an official edge. Not-offered is 200 with available:false.

POST /api/domains.note: Claim a domain. The edge looks the owner's TXT and CNAME records up itself and routes the domain once both are there. 400 for a name that is not one, 409 with the edge's sentence when the box has no ready Stripe account, has five domains already, or the domain is live for another box. Audited.

POST /api/domains/remove.note: Give a domain up; its route and certificate go at the next reconcile. Audited.

POST /api/domains/wallet.note:
Bind the box's wallet to its names: the edge checks the signature (personal_sign of "LosOS box name v1
zone: <zone>
box: <box>
address: <address>
") and publishes the ENS record at `names` in its DNSSEC-signed zone, so wallets that send to ENS names pay the box by name. {} takes it off. 400 for a bad address or a signature from another wallet. Audited.

GET /api/backup.note: The bucket without its secret key, the last backup (`/var/lib/losos-backup/last.json`), the backup or restore job, an erase under way with `secondsLeft` and `cancellable`, the report the last erase left (kept past the wipe in `/var/lib/losos-erase`), and the countdown length. Nothing set up is 200 with nulls.

GET /api/credentials.note: Every credential in /etc/credstore.encrypted that modules/credentials.nix declares, without its value. Admin only.

POST /api/credentials/{name}/rotate.note: Make a new value for a credential the box makes itself, seal it and restart its readers. 404 for an unknown name, 409 for one the box does not make or that cannot change. The value is never in the answer. Audited.

POST /api/backup/target.note: Set the S3 bucket backups go to (backend/src/backup.rs). https, or http only for a LAN address; bucket, folder, region and keys checked by shape; a Glacier storage class only on an amazonaws.com address. 400 with the field named; 409 while a backup or restore runs. The secret is written to /var/secrets (0600) and never answered. Audited.

DELETE /api/backup/target.note: Forget the bucket. The backups in it stay. 409 while a job runs or an erase is backing up to it. Audited.

POST /api/backup/run.note: Start a backup as the transient unit `losos-backup-<job>`: restic to the bucket, encrypted on the box with the recovery code as the repository password, keeping the last seven. 400 with no bucket; 409 while a job, a rebuild or an erase runs. Audited.

POST /api/backup/restore.note: Restore the newest backup in the bucket, opened with the recovery code of the box that made it (`losos-backup-<job>` running losos-restore). The code becomes this box's recovery code and the restored settings are applied by a rebuild when the job is done. 400 for a code that is not one or no bucket; 409 as for a backup. A wrong code fails the job with "the recovery code does not open this backup". Audited.

POST /api/erase.note: Start erasing the box (backend/src/erase.rs): an optional backup, a countdown of `losos.reset.graceMinutes`, then the edge is left (custom domains removed, a wallet bound to the box's names unbound, active listings closed, `/deregister`), the settings are put back, and the box restarts; `losos-factory-wipe.service` deletes the data early in the next boot. 400 for a backup with no bucket; 409 while anything else runs. Audited.

POST /api/erase/cancel.note: Stop an erase while it is backing up or counting down, or dismiss one whose backup failed; nothing has changed by then. 409 once the box has started leaving its edge. Audited.

POST /api/look.note: Choose a shipped picture, none, or the veil. Choosing anything but the upload removes the uploaded picture's bytes. 400 with the reason for an unknown name or a veil out of range. Not audited and not a rebuild: the look is a document, not a setting.

PUT /api/look/background.in: the picture's bytes, Content-Type image/png|jpeg|webp|gif|svg+xml, at most limits.imageBytes
PUT /api/look/background.note: Upload a background of your own.
